title: Role of Heat Treatment Atmosphere on the Microstructure and Surface Morphology of DLP-Fabricated High-Entropy Alloy Components.

recollection.starting_material: Digital Light Processing (DLP) additively manufactured high-entropy alloy green bodies, probably based on a common equiatomic CoCrFeNi (±Mn or Mo) powder feedstock suspended in a photopolymer resin
recollection.intervention: Post-printing heat treatments carried out in different atmospheres (high vacuum, flowing Ar, flowing N2, and laboratory air) at one or more temperatures in the 1000–1200 °C range for 1–2 h followed by furnace or gas quenching
recollection.structure: Vacuum/Ar heat treatments retained a single-phase FCC matrix with modest grain growth; N2 produced surface Cr-rich nitride precipitates; air caused formation of mixed oxides (Cr2O3, spinels) and a rough, up-to-10 µm thick oxide scale. Grain size roughly doubled in air but increased only ~30 % in inert atmospheres
recollection.mechanism: Atmospheric oxygen or nitrogen reacted with the high-entropy alloy during annealing, driving selective oxidation/nitridation of Cr (and possibly Mn) that disrupted the originally homogeneous solid solution; inert atmospheres suppressed interfacial reactions and limited elemental segregation, while oxygen promoted outward diffusion of Cr/Mn and oxide scale growth
recollection.results: Best (vacuum/Ar) condition showed ~15 % increase in Vickers hardness (to ≈ 280–300 HV) and <5 % change in surface roughness (Ra ≈ 4 µm). Air-annealed parts exhibited ~40 % higher surface roughness (Ra ≈ 9 µm) and a 10–12 % drop in tensile ductility. Nitrogen atmosphere gave intermediate properties with a slight hardness bump (≈ 290 HV) but reduced elongation due to brittle nitrides.

score.note: The recollection only broadly identifies atmosphere-dependent heat treatment and oxidation-related morphology changes. It incorrectly specifies alloy composition, atmospheres, treatment duration, phases, and properties, missing the air-versus-oxygen-deficient debinding comparison, residual-carbon/gas-evolution mechanism, sintering schedule, cracking and layer-removal behavior, and all reported oxygen, carbon, strength, and temperature values.
